punchline: Frank Lloyd Wright's apprentices paid him and worked in the fields in return.
thirty_sec: Adam Grant uses Frank Lloyd Wright as an example of a taker's long-term cost. Wright charged the young architects who wanted to work with him, had them do farm work and kept the credit for himself. The talented apprentices left once they saw they were not valued. Wright's genius was intact, but the people who could turn his ideas into reality were no longer with him.
